blocks.content: Suppose data are drawn from a normal distribution with a known mean, $ \mu $, but unknown variance, $ \sigma^{2} $. The resulting likelihood function can be expressed as $$ \ell(\sigma^{2}\mid\mathbf{x},\mu)\propto(\sigma^{2})^{-n/2}\exp\left(-\frac{nS^{2}}{2\sigma^{2}}\right) $$ where $$ S^{2}=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\left(x_{i}-\mu\right)^{2} $$

Notice that since we condition on x and μ (i.e., their values are known), $ S^2 $ is a constant. Further observe that, as a function of the unknown variance, $ \sigma^2 $, the likelihood is proportional to a scaled inverse $ \chi^2 $ distribution (Equation A2.30a).
